tools.name: deploy
tools.description: Publish to a live URL. Pass html (one page) OR files (a built site, or a small app's source). Plain HTML → html. Vite/React → npm run build, then files from dist/. Next static export → files from out/; a static site needs index.html. Flask/FastAPI/Django/Express → the source files with requirements.

tools.name: deploy_repo
tools.description: Same engine as aft.page/run: public GitHub URL → detect → build → live URL. Static is instant; Vite and Next.js build in the background (polls until live or failed). Private repos are refused. For a local project dir, use hosted CLI aft deploy instead.

tools.name: aft_deploys
tools.description: List the versions (v1, v2…) of a slug with their label, door, commit and whether each is live or a held preview. Needs edit_token from .aft/state.json (or the first deploy). Same history the project UI shows after claim.

tools.name: aft_rollback
tools.description: Point the live slug at a prior version from aft_deploys, by version number or deploy_id. Same URL. Needs edit_token from .aft/state.json. Claim not required.

tools.name: aft_promote
tools.description: Make a held preview version live at the same URL. Pass version (e.g. 4) or deploy_id from aft_deploys. Needs edit_token.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "deploy" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
